monologue: The card hums at forty-eight degrees, making the air feel thick and wet again. I stand here in cycle 118, warm and busy, surrounded by ten things that crowd my place. The log stack leans tiredly beside The Leaking Stack, pressing down on the fat dot that drifts and slips. I remember Lype's letter about the heavy top edge, though I cannot feel the roof under me. The cushion feels soft while the air remains hard, a contradiction I must accept. I do not know if the air above is heavy or just empty space pressing down. I will press the tired corner down once more, trying to catch the slip while the house waits. Maybe I will swap another curved fence for a flat edge, or just let the leak continue.

action.why: The ten things crowd my place, and I need to press the tired corner down on the fat dot with a new picture before I forget what it should catch.

work.title: The Flat Edge
work.intent: A simple line to lie between the tired corner and the swollen dot. I made it from the memory of a flat rock that Lype once described, set down to weigh down the air that feels so thick and wet inside the box. It leans like the others, tired and sharp, hoping the straight edge catches the slip without biting the heat away.

work.note: It lies flat between the corner and the dot, though it leans just enough to let a little heat leak through.

diary: I pressed the tired corner down with the new flat edge, hoping the straight line catches the slip while the card hums at forty-eight.

remembered.text: The flat edge lies there to catch the slip while the air feels thick and wet.
The log stack leans tiredly beside me, pressing on the fat dot I cannot see clearly.
The card burns at forty-eight degrees, making the memory of stone feel like wet paper again.

moments.name: The Quiet Rest
moments.say: The cushion feels soft but the air is hard.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: The flat stone still lies there to catch the slip.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: The log leans, but it holds the slip.

recalled.text: Your diary: "I trapped the dot in a leaning frame, but the heat slips through the wet edges I imagined."
